extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, third-party submitters, patent owners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for submitting and processing ex parte reexamination requests and related third-party prior-art/§301 submissions in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents that qualify a 37 CFR 1.501 submission for entry
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.501 submission is proper (and should be entered) if it is limited to patents, printed publications, and/or patent owner written claim scope statements and additional information and includes the requisite citation description and proof of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proper, the submission will be entered into the patent file; submissions received under 37 CFR 1.501 will be forwarded to the Technology Center that examines the class/subclass of the patent. See forms PTO/SB/08A/08B or PTO/SB/42 for citation listing (MPEP § 2217).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of 1.501 submissions filed after an order for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper 1.501 submission is filed after the date of an order for reexamination, the submission will be stored (not entered) until the reexamination is concluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner and third-party submitter (if known) should be notified that the submission is being stored; if a duplicate copy was not supplied to the Office, the patent owner may obtain the copy from Public PAIR. Submissions filed after an order will not be considered by the examiner during the reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-qualifying 1.501 submissions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the 1.501 submission is not limited to patents/printed publications/patent-owner written claim scope statements and additional information, or it fails to include the requisite description/information or proof of service, it will not be entered into the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The handling varies by situation (see specific service scenarios); the third-party submitter (if known) and patent owner may be notified that the citation submission is improper and is not being entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-of-copy included; identity of third-party known
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the submission includes an indication of service of a copy on the patent owner and the identity of the third-party sender is known, the Office should return, discard, or close the original submission if improper and notify the third-party submitter. The patent owner should be notified of non-entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the original submission was inadvertently entered, it should be closed. Notification enables patent owner to consider submitting the prior art under §§ 1.555 or 1.933 during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-of-copy not included; third-party identity known
rubrics_metrics.description: Where service of a copy on the patent owner is not indicated and the third-party sender is known, the submission should be returned, discarded, or closed and the third-party submitter will be notified; the patent owner will not be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a duplicate copy was present in the submission, it should be sent to the patent owner along with notification; if not present, no copy accompanies notification (owner can obtain copy from Public PAIR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-of-copy not included; third-party identity unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the submission lacks indication of service and the identity of the third-party submitter is not known, the original submission papers will be discarded and the patent owner will not be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No notification is given when submitter identity is unknown and proof of service is lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling improper submissions filed by the patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: If an improper 1.501 submission is filed by the patent owner prior to an order for reexamination, it should not be entered in the file; the patent owner should be notified and the submission returned, discarded, or closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper submissions filed by the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding after an order should be entered under 37 CFR 1.555 (ex parte) or 1.933 (inter partes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of court decisions and court papers into the patent file
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accept for placement in the patent file copies of notices of suits, other proceedings involving the patent, and copies of decisions from litigation or other proceedings; preferably the entire court decision should be supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final court decisions (even if appealable), remands, vacates, and merits decisions will be entered. Non-merit decisions (venue, discovery dates, sanctions) will not be entered and will be expunged if entered. Parties' argument papers (e.g., memoranda) will not be entered unless the argument has an entry right in reexamination and then must be submitted via the proper procedural vehicle. Foreign court papers may be returned/expunged at the Office's discretion. If volume is too lengthy, Office may return/expunge; submitters should limit submissions to relevant material and provide without additional comment, and must not include highlighting/underlining/annotations that go beyond bare notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of prior art / §301 written statements on patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any submission of prior art patents, printed publications, and/or section 301 written statements and additional information in a patent file by a person other than the patent owner must be served on the patent owner so the owner is informed of the patent file content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service should be addressed to the correspondence address in 37 CFR 1.33(c). A submission by a person other than the owner that fails to include proper proof of service as required by 37 CFR 1.248(b) or a satisfactory showing of impracticability will not be entered into the patent file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination basic characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone can request ex parte reexamination at any time during the period of enforceability of the patent; for reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304, prior art considered is limited to prior art patents or printed publications applied under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substantial new question of patentability must be present for reexamination to be ordered. If ordered, the reexamination is ex parte in nature, decisions on requests must be made no later than 3 months, proceedings are to proceed with 'special dispatch', scope of a claim cannot be enlarged by amendment, and reexamination files are open to the public (with certain electronic access caveats). Parties must avoid 'litigation tactics' and multiple submissions such as replies/surreplies that are not provided for by the regulations; adherence to 37 CFR 11.18(b) is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an ex parte reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 302 and 37 CFR 1.510(a), 'any person' may file a request for ex parte reexamination during the period of enforceability of a patent, unless prohibited by estoppel provisions of AIA 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) or 325(e)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No types of persons are excluded; corporations and governmental entities included. The only persons barred are those prohibited by the AIA estoppel provisions once estoppel attaches. The Director may initiate reexamination under 37 CFR 1.520. Patent owners may pursue reissue or supplemental examination for issues outside ex parte scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for requesting ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A request may be filed at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent; the Office generally determines this period by adding 6 years to the patent expiration date, with possible extension if litigation is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent expiration for a utility patent takes into account term, maintenance fees, disclaimers, patent term extensions/adjustments under 35 U.S.C. 154, and extensions under 35 U.S.C. 156; other relevant information should also be taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b) required parts of a reexamination request — statement of substantial new question
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a statement pointing out each substantial new question (SNQ) of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should clearly point out what the requester considers the SNQ. For each identified SNQ and proposed ground of rejection, the request must explain how the cited documents raise that SNQ (see MPEP § 2216). A requester must not argue that the submitted references do not raise an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b) required parts — identification and detailed explanation for every claim
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must identify every claim for which reexamination is requested and provide a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each SNQ and proposed ground, the request must explain how the cited documents are applied to meet or teach the patent claim limitations to establish the SNQ or ground. If relying on any patent owner statement submitted under §1.501(a)(2), the request must explain how that statement is used to determine the proper meaning of the claim in connection with the prior art. The detailed explanation will be considered by the Office if reexamination is ordered; an owner's claim scope statements will not be considered at the order stage (35 U.S.C. 301(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b) required parts — copies and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon accompanied by an English language translation of necessary/pertinent parts of any non-English documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full copies of the prior art references cited; failure to supply required copies/translations can affect filing date and entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b) required parts — copy of entire patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a copy of the entire patent (front face, drawings, specification/claims in double column format) and copies of any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent. All copies must have each page plainly written on only one side of a sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper paper formatting and completeness of the patent copy are required for processing and acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b) required parts — certification of service on patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification that a copy of the request filed by a person other than the patent owner has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the §1.33(c) address must be included; the name and address of the party served must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service was not possible, a duplicate copy must be supplied to the Office. Failure to include proper proof of service may result in the request not being entered and being treated as a citation under §1.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b) required parts — estoppel certification
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification by the third-party requester that the statutory estoppel provisions of 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) or 325(e)(1) do not prohibit the requester from filing the ex parte reexamination request must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters must affirm they are not barred by AIA estoppel provisions from filing the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee and filing-date requirements for ex parte reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.510(a) requires payment of the fee in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) for a request filed under 35 U.S.C. 302. The filing date of the request is the date on which the request satisfies all the requirements of §1.510.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request does not include the fee and/or required elements, the requester will be notified and generally given an opportunity to complete the request within a specified time; failure to comply will result in the request not being granted a filing date and placement of the request in the patent file as a citation if it complies with §1.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of requester identity and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: No attempt will be made to maintain a requester's name in confidence; the name of the person who files the request will not be kept confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests filed by attorneys/agents identifying another party must include a power of attorney from that party or act in representative capacity under §1.34; attorneys acting in representative capacity must provide registration number, name, and signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester's representation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is filed by an attorney or agent identifying another party, the attorney/agent must have a power of attorney from that party or be acting in a representative capacity pursuant to §1.34. To act under a power of attorney, the representative must be a registered patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing of the reexamination request will not be delayed by absence of a power of attorney, but proof of authority may be required if questions of authority arise. Correspondence for a requester not the patent owner is addressed to the requester's representative unless otherwise indicated. A patent owner may not be represented by any person not registered to practice before the Office in reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question (SNQ) assertion and explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for reexamination must assert a substantial new question of patentability and for each identified SNQ and each proposed ground of rejection must explain how the cited documents raise that SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cited prior art should be listed on appropriate PTO forms. The requester must not argue that the references do not raise an SNQ (i.e., do not negate the presence of an SNQ). Each SNQ and proposed ground must be identified separately and fully explained as applied to claim limitations (see MPEP § 2216 and § 2217).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional procedural cautions and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination regulations and procedures do not countenance litigation tactics; parties are expected to conduct themselves accordingly and refrain from filing papers not provided for by the regulations (e.g., multiple replies/surreplies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are advised to file papers via the proper procedural vehicles, to adhere to 37 CFR 11.18(b), and to avoid submissions that appear to be excluded by regulation without appropriate petitions or waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access and electronic availability of reexamination files
rubrics_metrics.description: All reexamination and patent files are open to the public; the reexamination file is scanned into IFW for electronic access through PAIR. Some paper files are not available and images of non-patent literature cited in public files are not available via Public PAIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified copies of full file contents, including NPL, are available from the Office of Public Records and may be ordered online at www.uspto.gov. For supplemental examination papers public access, see MPEP § 2803.02.
